questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells drivers to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers or pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: When is pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first starts to fall.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts to fall.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Oil and dirt on the road mix with water to create a slick, greasy surface.

questions.question: What is the 'No zone'?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the 'No zone.'

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, where should you drive?

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the center line.
Left of the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the center line.
questions.explanation: To turn left from a two-way street, stay in the lane closest to the center line. Begin your turn just before you reach the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first available legal lane.

questions.question: Which lane should you use before turning left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: To turn, use the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night driving
Uphill driving

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds increase how far it takes to stop and make crashes worse. The faster you drive, the harder your car will hit in a crash.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
Neither more nor less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see, headlight glare can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: If a red light shows a green arrow, when can you proceed in that direction?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes to green.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane. The arrow overrides other signals. Always yield to pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way rules?

options.text: Assume all drivers will follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers will follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up your right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up your right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you automatically have the right-of-way. Consider what is happening at the intersection. Be willing to let others go if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces the effect of alcohol.
It has no effect on driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can impair your driving. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes the danger worse and increases your crash risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road has curves ahead.

questions.question: You should allow extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see the back of their vehicle.
A small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see the back of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles with trailers may not see you behind them. Stay farther back. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so increase your distance to see around them.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. A broken yellow line means you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Watch for children.

questions.question: Before turning left, it is important to:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and continue carefully.

questions.question: In rainy weather, be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with the rain and makes the road very slippery.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for trains from both directions.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Look for trains from both directions. Also watch for school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials, as they must stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.question: If the road ahead is covered by heavy smoke, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Slow down, move far to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move far to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If heavy smoke covers the road ahead, slow down right away. Drive as far to the right as possible and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can hurt your eyes, lungs, or be dangerous.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Slow down without braking hard and carefully steer back onto the road. Watch for other traffic before moving back onto the pavement.

questions.question: Using a cell phone to talk or text while driving does not increase your chances of being in a crash.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving distracts you and increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you must let all drivers who arrived before you go first.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to drivers who arrived before you. Wait your turn to enter the intersection.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Roads are slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra space when stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerous and slippery, especially right after it rains. Your tires sit on a thin layer of water, oil, and dirt. Slow down in heavy rain or standing water to keep traction.

questions.question: Highway work zones have become increasingly safe for workers and drivers.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Highway work zones have become increasingly dangerous for both workers and drivers.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean:

options.text: Neither lane can pass.
Both lanes can pass.
The lane to the right can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane can pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and look in all directions for traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Carefully drive around the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: You can drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These include flashing red lights, lowered gates, flaggers, or a train's horn. Do not drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Trucks have larger blind spots than cars.
Avoid driving beside a large truck for long periods.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots behind the cab and along the entire length. The driver cannot see you there. Avoid staying beside or behind large trucks for long periods.
